title: Private Upgrade Concierge: staged, transactional migrations with LTS-aware rollout gates
creator: Anita Gomez
description:
Build an "Upgrade Concierge" tool for Redwood Private that orchestrates multi-stage, transactional upgrades and schema migrations across VPC/on-prem clusters. The Concierge will coordinate Helm/agent upgrades, database schema runners, KV cache compatibility transforms, and per-node rollback checkpoints while enforcing LTS channel policies and rollout gates. Goals:

- Provide a safe, observable path for customers to move between LTS and non-LTS channel versions with minimal downtime.
- Orchestrate coordinated steps (preflight -> canary cohort -> ramp -> verify -> finalize) with automatic and manual gates.
- Support dry-run/plan mode that simulates migrations against snapshots and emits an actionable plan.
- Expose pause/resume/abort hooks and a deterministic rollback strategy for in-flight upgrades.
- Integrate telemetry and post-upgrade regression checks (prompt sets/evals) to gate finalization.

Scope (this ticket): implement the core orchestration engine, gating primitives, and Helm + DB migration adapters for the most common Private deployment topology (control-plane + 3 worker pools). Not in scope: full tenant-aware multi-tenant rewrites, advanced migration translators for bespoke customer schemas (follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Concierge can produce a dry-run plan for a sample private cluster and persist the plan to S3/Drive (link).
Runbook steps and automated gates are visible in Console (rollout timeline + per-node status).
Support a canary cohort (single worker pool) upgrade and automatic fallback on failed health probes within configured timeout.
Transactional DB migration step supports dry-run and reversible markers; a failed migration must trigger a safe abort with state restoration where possible.
Audit logs for every step are emitted with operator identity and KMS-wrapped secrets where applicable.
Post-upgrade quality checks (basic evals) run automatically and can block finalization when regressions exceed threshold.
comments: 2025-01-12 - Spike: validated Helm 3.9 hooks for pre/post upgrade tasks on a 3-node private cluster; discovered delays when draining KV cache (notes in Confluence: /d/UpgradeConcierge/spike-helm-drain).

2025-01-15 - Design review with Infra and Security: agreed to require KMS envelope for migration keys and to limit agent-upgrade concurrency by default (configurable). Action: add KMS integration story.
2025-01-20 - Engineering sync: implemented first prototype of gating primitive (time-window + success-rate check). CI runs flaky; increased unit-test timeouts for e2e harness.
2025-01-24 - QA: dry-run plan validated against anonymized snapshot; found edge-case with CRD upgrade ordering. Created follow-up ENG-47311 to sequence CRD migrations.
2025-01-30 - Security review stubbed: need a formal threat model for the rollback channel (ticket created with Security).

2025-02-03 - Canary test: performed a limited canary on staging-priv-01; observed a 0.6s median increase in per-request tail latency during warmup; telemetry indicates KV-cache re-warm dominates. Planning: introduce staggered cache warmup and pre-population in next sprint.
decision_log: 2025-01-14 - Decision: prefer orchestrator-driven Helm upgrades (control-plane triggering helm/operator) vs agent-only approach to enable cross-pool coordination. Rationale: cross-node ordering and centralized rollback are simpler with orchestration. (trade-off: operator installation complexity).
2025-01-18 - Decision: require a dry-run pass for any LTS-bound rollout; dry-run failures are blocking by default. Rationale: LTS channel implies higher safety guarantees.
2025-01-25 - Decision: initial rollback strategy will be stateful where possible (db migration reversible markers); when not reversible, Concierge will halt and require manual intervention.
